'''Sir George Charles Radda''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS}} ({{langx|hu|Radda György Károly}}; 9 June 1936 – 13 September 2024) was a Hungarian-British chemist. 

== Biography ==
Radda was born in Hungary on 9 June 1936.<ref name=Birth>{{cite web|title=Birthday's today|url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/archive/2011-6-9.html |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110610141354/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/archive/2011-6-9.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= 10 June 2011 |work=The Telegraph|access-date=2 June 2014|date=9 June 2011|quote=Prof Sir George Radda, Chief Executive, Medical Research Council, 1996–2003, 75 }}</ref> In 1957, he attended [[Merton College, Oxford]], to study [[chemistry]] and worked on electrophilic aromatic substitution with [[Richard Norman (chemist)|Richard Norman]] and [[Jeremy R. Knowles|Jeremy Knowles]],<ref>{{cite journal 
| doi= 10.1039/jr9600004885
| journal =J. Chem. Soc.
| first1 = J.R. |last1 =Knowles
| first2 = R.O.C. | last2 = Norman
| first3 = G. | last3 = Radda
| title = A quantitative treatment of electrophilic aromatic substitution
| year = 1960
| pages = 4885–4896
}}</ref> having set aside an earlier interest in [[literary criticism]].<ref name=NewSci /><ref name="heart">{{cite web|url=http://www.heartacademy.org/newsletter/4/4.pdf|title=''Heartacademy – Newsletter''|publisher=heartacademy.org|pages=3|access-date=27 January 2010|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924025429/http://www.heartacademy.org/newsletter/4/4.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> His early work was concerned with the development and use of fluorescent probes for the study of structure and function of membranes and enzymes. He became interested in using [[spectroscopy|spectroscopic]] methods including [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] (NMR) to study complex biological material.<ref name="heart"/> In 1974, his research paper was the first to introduce the use of NMR to study tissue metabolites. In 1981, he and his colleagues published the first scientific report on the clinical application of his work. This resulted in the installation of a magnet large enough to accommodate the whole human body for NMR investigations in 1983 at the [[John Radcliffe Hospital]] in [[Oxford]].<ref name="heart"/><ref>{{Cite journal
 | pmid = 21546958
| year = 2011
| last1 = Radda
| first1 = G
| title = Straight talk with...George Radda. Interview by David Cyranoski
| journal = Nature Medicine
| volume = 17
| issue = 5
| pages = 525
| doi = 10.1038/nm0511-525
| doi-access = free
}}</ref>

In 1982 Radda published work concerning the relationship between deoxygenated haemoglobin and the NMR signal.<ref>{{Cite Q | Q28264358 }}</ref>

From 1996 until his retirement in 2003, Radda was Chief Executive of the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] in the UK.<ref name='timesobit'>{{cite news |title=Professor Sir George Radda obituary, Hungarian refugee and scientific pioneer |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/obituaries/article/professor-sir-george-radda-obituary-hungarian-refugee-and-scientific-pioneer-pzlx5qwb3 |access-date=19 September 2024 |work=[[The Times]] |date=19 September 2024}}</ref> In 2009 he was appointed chairman of the [[Biomedical Research Council]] in [[Singapore]].<ref name='timesobit'/>

Radda died on 13 September 2024, at the age of 88.<ref>[https://www.vg.hu/vilaggazdasag-magyar-gazdasag/2024/09/elhunyt-radda-gyorgy-karoly-professzor Elhunyt Radda György Károly professzor] {{in lang|hu}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=MRI Pioneer Professor Sir George Radda Passes Away |url=https://hungarytoday.hu/mri-pioneer-professor-sir-george-radda-passes-away/ |access-date=16 September 2024 |work=Hungary Today |date=16 September 2024}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Radda received numerous prestigious awards and honours for his pioneering efforts in using spectroscopic techniques for metabolic studies, including a [[Buchanan Medal]] in 1987.<ref name="RSbuch" /> He was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[1993 Birthday Honours]] for services to science, and [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2000 Birthday Honours]] for services to biomedical science.<ref>United Kingdom: {{London Gazette |date=11 June 1993 |supp=y |issue=53332|pages=9 }}</ref><ref name=GB>United Kingdom: {{London Gazette |issue=55879 |date=19 June 2000 |pages=1  |supp=1 }}</ref>

In addition, he was a Fellow of [[Merton College, Oxford]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/fellows_and_research/honorary.shtml|title=Emeritus, Visiting and Honorary Fellows at Merton College, Oxford|publisher=Merton College, Oxford|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618061212/http://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/fellows_and_research/honorary.shtml|archive-date=18 June 2013|access-date=10 June 2013}}</ref> a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/uploadedFiles/Royal_Society_Content/about-us/fellowship/Fellows_and_Foreign_Members.pdf|title=Fellows of the Royal Society|date=13 April 2013|publisher=The Royal Society|access-date=10 June 2013}}</ref> and was a [[British Heart Foundation]] Professor of Molecular Cardiology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/ld200102/ldselect/ldanimal/999/1120402.htm|title=House of Lords – Animals in Scientific Procedures – Minutes of Evidence|publisher=UK Parliament|access-date=10 June 2013}}</ref> In 1998, he was an inaugural [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deceased Fellows |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/more-fellowship/deceased-fellows |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref> He was also awarded many distinguished prizes throughout his scientific career. He was an Honorary Member of the [[American Heart Association]]<ref name="heart" /> and was awarded the Citation for International Achievement.<ref name="heart" />

In 2015, he was conferred an award as an [[Honorary Citizen of Singapore]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/two-foreigners-made-honorary-citizens-of-spore|title=Two foreigners made Honorary Citizens of S'pore|last=Khew|first=Carolyn|date=22 October 2015|website=The Straits Times|language=en|access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref> 

In 2018 he was awarded the [[Hungarian Corvin Chain]]. This is the second highest Hungarian state decoration and is awarded to persons who have made an outstanding contribution to the improvement of Hungarian public thought, science and culture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dailynewshungary.com/hungarian-president-decorates-artists-academics-corvin-chain-award-merit/|title=Hungarian President decorates artists, academics with Corvin Chain Award for Merit|last=Béni|first=Alexandra|date=12 February 2018|website=Daily News Hungary/|language=en|access-date=4 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ferry |first=Georgina |date=2024-10-02 |title=Sir George Radda obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2024/oct/02/sir-george-radda-obituary |access-date=2024-10-07 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
